Electrochemical CO 2 reduction (ECO 2 R) holds immense potential for sustainable carbon conversion, yet the expedient synthesis of high-performance electrocatalysts remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a rapid Joule-heating approach to convert Cu(OH) 2 precursors into highly efficient Cu-based electrocatalysts for ECO 2 R, achieving superior catalyst preparation efficiency and catalytic performance compared with conventional tube-furnace annealing. Optimization of the F/Cu molar ratio (10:1) affords a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 61.7% toward C 2 products. In-situ spectroscopic and mechanistic analyses reveal that F incorporation increases surface *OH coverage and stabilizes *CHO/*CO intermediates, promoting efficient C–C coupling. This work utilizes Joule heating as a potentially scalable platform for designing Cu-based electrocatalysts with enhanced activity and stability toward CO 2 reduction to valuable C 2 chemicals.
